title: +91% realized in 2 weeks of live trading - my Python bot router (spot + leverage, 67k backtests, walk-forward OOS only). Full breakdown inside
author: blue_nairda

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 67k backtests is where I'd push back. a holdout only stays clean the first time you look at it. once you've kept the families that passed it and dropped the ones that didn't, the holdout has become part of your fitting too, and two weeks live can't separate those yet.

replies.author: blue_nairda
replies.body:
Yeah that's fair. But I've also been working on this for months. The two weeks is just how long it's been live with real money. The strategies I built and selected over a month ago have been rerun on all the data that came in since, and they've held up, so the holdout isn't the only out of sample check they've had at this point. But yeah, a month still isn't that much time. 

But that's also why I have the spot account. The leveraged bots are the risky part, high risk high reward, so the plan is to take a percentage of the profits from them and move it into spot on a schedule and keep some for myself. Spot can't get liquidated, so worst case the leveraged side goes to zero and I've already moved the profits out. I really only need one or two profitable months from the leveraged bots to make my initial money back, and after that it's running on profits. And second leveraged bot only runs strategies with stop losses, so that one can't get liquidated either, and if its live results start drifting from the backtest I'll know the strategies aren't holding up.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, rerunning the ones you picked a month ago on everything since is a real forward check, more than most posts here show. how many did you pick them from?

replies.author: blue_nairda
replies.body:
Each strategy came from a search of about 100k parameter combinations. The best \~600 of those get tested on 5 different holdout layouts, and the one that did best on the holdout is the one I trade.   
So the same strategy gets searched 5 separate times, each with a different holdout layout (after a date, before a date, a window in the middle, everything outside a window, alternating blocks), and I only use a strategy if it passed on all 5. Then on top of that, the 12 strategies the bots are running were picked from a few hundred searches per pair. All 12 were picked between Aug 10 and Aug 15 and they've held up on everything since.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 5 holdout layouts is more than most posts here do. the part I'd still worry about is picking the best of a few hundred searches per pair, that pick alone makes a holdout look good. how close is the 2 weeks live to what the holdouts said?

replies.author: blue_nairda
replies.body: I just pulled the latest market data and reran the backtest for every strategy the bots are currently running, through today. Win rate and trade size are in line with the backtest: the backtest shows 100% winners over the same period, live is 25 of 26 with one stop-loss, and the trades are a similar size. The holdout win rates for these strategies were 96–100%, so live is in line with the holdouts.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the thing I'd check is how big that one stop was next to the average win. 100% winners usually means a close target and a far stop, so a single loss can undo a lot of wins. I built Quantradin for exactly this, it grades a strategy with take-profit left out of the score. free, paper only, it's on my profile.

replies.author: blue_nairda
replies.body:
Just to be clear these are three separate bots, and the one stop was on the spot bot.

Spot bot: 13 trades, 12 wins, 1 stop. The wins averaged +1.48% of position, the smallest was +0.42%, the biggest +4.73%. The stop was −0.28%. So the loss was smaller than every single win, about a fifth of the average one. Not a close target and far stop situation, at least not in what's actually hit so far.

For context, the other two bots are leveraged. One without stop losses is 11 for 11, averaging +5.6% of position. The one with stop losses went live 4 days ago, it's 2 for 2 averaging +5.9%, and no stop has triggered on it yet.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: ok that's a better split than I assumed, a stop at a fifth of the average win is fine. my worry was the backtest side: 100% winners there usually means the stop never got hit in testing, so live is the first time you learn how it behaves.

replies.author: blue_nairda
replies.body:
**Correction and additional context:**  
  
The stop-loss I mentioned earlier wasn't technically a stop, it was a time-out exit at breakeven that cost −0.28% after fees and slippage. I just double checked and the most up to date backtest has the same time-out exit on the same day at −0.12% after fees. It didn't count it as a stop-loss. So the spot bot technically it is still matching the backtest and holdout.  
  
Additional Context (from original post):

* One bot runs many strategies at once (different pairs, timeframes and families). Whatever fires first opens the position. If another strategy fires while a position is open, it's tracked virtually; when the real position closes, the router picks up the still-open virtual trade if it's within a threshold of its entry, generally −3%, so it doesn't chase a trade that already ran.
* Three bots live right now: a spot router, a leverage router that only runs stop-less strategies, and a second leverage router that only runs strategies with stop-losses.
* Leverage is 3–8x isolated, sized per strategy from the backtest.

The spot bot is running 9 different strategies across 5 pairs. All of the spot strategies had a 96–100% win rate in the backtests.
